sentences.text: Shri Amit Dubey with Shri L.P.Singh, Advocate for the applicants.

Shri Rajesh Tiwari, G.A. with Shri Ajay Tamrakar, P.L. for the
respondent/State.

Whether approved for reporting : (Yes/No).
 O R D E R (28.06.2018) This revision petition under section 397/401 of the Cr.P.C. has been preferred on behalf of the applicants against the order dated 4.2.2013 passed by the court of Judicial Magistrate Class I, Hoshangabad in Criminal Case No.205/2010 whereby charges under sections 7(i) read with section 16(1),(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
have been framed against the applicants with regard to selling of adulterated Achar Masala.

2. Facts giving rise to the present case, briefly stated, are that on 28.11.2008 Food Inspector Jeewan Singh Rajak has inspected the shop of Sai Kripa Super Bazar situated at Meenakshi Chowk,
Hoshangabad of which the applicant no.2 was the Proprietor.
The Food Inspector took samples of Divya Garam Masala, Muneem Ji Ag- mark Great 1 Dhaniya Powder and Ramdev Achar Garam Masala from the applicant no.1 and sent for analysis.
As per the Analyst re- port, sample of Ramdev Achar Masala was found to be adulterated.
Thereafter, the sanction was obtained and the case was filed on 24.2.2010.
On examination of the sample of Ramdev Achar Masala from the Central Food Laboratory also as per section 13(2) of the Act, the same was found again found to be adulterated.
Thereafter, vide order dated 4.2.2013 charges have been framed against the appli- cants.

3. Learned counsel for the applicants have assailed the proceed- ings of framing of charge on the Vinay Jaiswal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88727584/
1 ground that applicants no.1 and 2 had purchased the Achar Masala from the applicant no.3 and the ap- plicant no.3 has purchased the same from Ramdev Products Private Limited, who is accused no.4 before the court below.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicants have submitted purchasing bills to the Food Inspector and the Achar Masala was purchased under the warrantee as mentioned in the bill.
Therefore, as per the provisions of section 19(2) of the Act, the appli- cants, being the vendor, cannot be prosecuted for commission of the offence.
Apart from it, it is also contended that sample was taken on 28.11.2008 and the complaint was filed on 24.2.2010.
The delay caused in filing of the complaint prejudiced the applicants; hence, they were deprived to send another sample to the Central Food Labo- ratory for analysis.

Learned counsel has further contended that at the stage of framing of charge, if there is material to establish the plea taken by the applicants accused, they may be exonerated as has been laid down by this Court in the case of Gulabchand Modi Vs. State of M.P.,
reported in 2005(1) M.P.H.T. 394 and Puranmal and an- other vs. State of M.P. and others, reported in (2007(1) M.P.L.J.
90).

sentences.text: Therefore, the charge and the proceedings be quashed and set aside.
4. On the other hand, learned G.A. opposed the aforesaid con- tentions and stated that section 19 of the Act came into operation with regard to defence of the vender during the trial.

For ready refer- ence, section 19(2) of the Act is quoted hereinbelow :-
19. Defences which may or may not be allowed in prosecutions under this Act.--

(1) It shall be no defence in a prosecution for an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated or misbranded article of food to allege merely that the vendor was ignorant of the nature, substance or quality of the food sold by him or that the purchaser having purchased any article for analysis was not prejudiced by the sale.

[(2) A vendor shall not be deemed to have committed an offence pertaining to the sale of any adulterated or misbranded article of food if he proves-- (a) that he purchased the article of food-- (i) in a case where a licence is prescribed for the sale thereof, from a duly licensed manufacturer,
distributor or dealer,
(ii) in any other case, from any manufacturer, distributor or dealer, with a written warranty in the prescribed form; and (b) that the article of food while in his possession was properly stored and that he sold it in the same state as he purchased it.]
(3) Any person by whom a warranty as is referred to 2[in section 14] is alleged to have been given shall be entitled to appear at the hearing and give evidence.
5. In the present case, it has to be proved by the applicants that they have purchased the food articles from accused Ramdev Food Products.

In this case it is not admitted on behalf of the accused Vinay Jaiswal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 28 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88727584/
2 no.4 that the article was sold under the warrantee and, therefore, proceed- ings cannot be closed against the applicants.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the petition be dismissed.

6. Having considered the contentions advanced by learned coun- sel for the parties and on perusal of the record, in view of this Court in the present case there is no evidence or admission on behalf of Ramdev Food Products Private Limited that the articles were sold to the applicant no.3.

Therefore,
in this case the plea taken by appli- cants no.1 to 3 is required to be proved.
The provision of section 19 of the Act provides an opportunity to raise a defence of such a nature during the trial.
Merely taking a plea of such a nature by the vendor proceedings cannot be quashed deeming that the vendor has not committed any offence.

7. So far as the aforesaid judgment in the case of Gulabchand and Puranmal (supra) are concerned,
in the aforesaid cases, the aforesaid plea taken on behalf of the vendor was admitted by the seller or man- ufacturer and the case was pending for a long time.
Therefore, the charges were quashed.
In the present case, in view of the provisions of section 19 of the Act and differentiation on the factual grounds, both the judgments are not relevant to the present case.

8. The contention that on account of delay in filing of the com- plaint, the applicants are prejudiced,
is not significant as there is no material before this Court to hold that the alleged article was of such a nature that after a lapse of the aforesaid time it became unfit for re- analysis by the Central Food Laboratory and on behalf of the appli- cants no efforts were made to pursue the right available under section 13 of the Act.
Therefore, merely on the aforesaid grounds the charge and the proceedings cannot be quashed.

9. Hence, in view of the discussions, this revision petition is dis- missed, being devoid of merit with a liberty to the applicants to raise all the questions before the trial court during trial at appropriate stage.
If such objection is raised, the trial court shall decide the same without being prejudiced by the observations made in this order.
Consequently, interim order dated 9.10.2013 passed by this Court stands vacated.
10. A copy of this order be sent to the court concerned for informa- tion and compliance.
